items.title: Amazon in talks to buy AI-compute startup Decart for about $7B, WSJ reports
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports Amazon is negotiating to acquire Decart, an AI startup whose software runs AI workloads across Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs and Amazon's Trainium chips, in a deal valued at about $7 billion. The deal could close soon if talks hold, but another bidder could still emerge. Anthropic had been in talks at about $6B but walked away after due diligence in September.
items.why_it_matters: A $7B purchase would be a large bid by AWS for cross-chip inference software, aimed at easing Trainium adoption against Nvidia's software lock-in.

items.title: ByteDance, Tencent rush personal AI agents after Meta's Muse; Caixin cover story on China's shift to agents
items.summary: Caixin Global reports on 12 Oct that ByteDance and Tencent are fast-tracking personal AI agents following the success of Meta's Muse assistant, with ByteDance reportedly speeding up a personal agent for its Doubao assistant ahead of the National Day holiday. A companion Caixin cover story says Tencent, Alibaba and ByteDance are betting that office-task enterprise agents (Tencent's WorkBuddy, ByteDance's Doubao Work) will reshape workplace software, while adoption and business models remain uncertain.
items.why_it_matters: Signals China's big platforms are pivoting from chatbots to consumer and enterprise agents, mirroring the US Muse-driven shift.
